prompts.eco.problem.short: Help me define the problem for a project on [topic] in [place].
prompts.eco.problem.detailed: I want to do a project on [topic] in [place: school, neighbourhood, city]. What I've noticed: [observations]. Help me define the problem: who it affects, how it shows up, why it matters, what can be measured. Suggest 3 versions at different scales and mark which one [who: a class, a team] could realistically tackle.
prompts.eco.problem.refine: Make version [number] more specific: where, when, how much.
prompts.eco.problem.check: My problem statement: [problem]. How can I check it's not just my impression?
prompts.eco.data.short: How can I collect verifiable data on [problem]?
prompts.eco.data.detailed: I need data on [problem] in [place]. Suggest 3 ways to collect it: observation, counting or measuring, open official data. For each: exactly what to record, how often, what table to log it in, what errors are possible. No collecting personal data or photos of people without consent.
prompts.eco.data.refine: We only have [time] to collect data. How can we keep the sample small but fair?
prompts.eco.data.check: Here's our data collection plan: [plan]. What could skew the results?
prompts.eco.survey.short: Write a survey on [topic] without collecting personal data
prompts.eco.survey.detailed: Write an anonymous survey on “[topic]” for [audience]. 8–10 questions: multiple choice, 1–5 scales, 1–2 open-ended. Don't ask for names, contact details, exact addresses, specific class names or anything else that could identify someone. Keep questions neutral, without hinting at a “right” answer. Add an intro: why the survey and that it's anonymous.
prompts.eco.survey.refine: Question [number] is leading. Rewrite it neutrally.
prompts.eco.survey.check: Could someone be identified from the combination of answers in my survey? [questions]
prompts.eco.campaign.short: Help me plan an awareness campaign on [topic] for [audience].
prompts.eco.campaign.detailed: A campaign on [topic] for [audience] over [time]. Resources: [resources]. Make a plan: one key message, 3 specific actions we want people to take, channels (a stand, school social media, a mini lesson, posters), a schedule, how we'll know it worked. Respectful tone, no shaming or scaring.
prompts.eco.campaign.refine: Come up with 5 short slogan options for the campaign.
prompts.eco.campaign.check: How can we measure the campaign's impact without collecting personal data?
prompts.eco.materials.short: Make a materials list for [event or project].
prompts.eco.materials.detailed: I need a materials list for [event or project], about [number] participants. Table: item, quantity, where to get it (school, bring from home, ask partners, buy), who's responsible (by role). Mark reusable alternatives to disposable items.
prompts.eco.materials.refine: Cut the list down to the bare essentials.
prompts.eco.materials.check: Which items might be hazardous or need adult supervision?
prompts.eco.solutions.detailed: Problem: [problem]. Possible solutions: [solutions]. Table: solution, what's needed, cost (relative), time to results, who needs to be involved, possible side effects, how to measure success. Where effectiveness is unknown, say so. Finish with which solution is realistic for us.
prompts.eco.solutions.refine: Could solutions [numbers] be combined? What would that look like?
prompts.eco.solutions.check: We chose [solution]. Who might object, and why?
prompts.eco.volunteer.short: Help me plan a volunteer event: [what we're doing]
prompts.eco.volunteer.detailed: Event: [what we're doing], venue: [type of place, no exact address], [number] participants, date [date]. Plan: what to agree in advance and with whom (by role), volunteer roles, safety briefing, materials, a timed programme, a bad-weather plan, how to wrap up. Don't collect more participant data than needed.
prompts.eco.volunteer.refine: Write a short invitation for participants without unnecessary detail.
prompts.eco.volunteer.check: What risks might we have missed? [plan]
prompts.eco.conclusions.short: What conclusions can be drawn from this data: [data]?
prompts.eco.conclusions.detailed: We collected data: [data]. Method: [method], number of observations: [number]. Help me phrase conclusions: what the data shows confidently, what it only hints at, what it can't show. Suggest careful wording like “in our sample” instead of “everyone” and “always”.
prompts.eco.conclusions.refine: What additional data would make the conclusion [conclusion] more reliable?
prompts.eco.conclusions.check: My conclusion: [conclusion]. Am I overstating it?
prompts.eco.claims.short: Which claims in my text need sources? [text]
prompts.eco.claims.detailed: Read the project text and list the claims that need a source: numbers, comparisons, causes, forecasts, “scientists have proven”. Table: claim, why it needs a source, what kind of source would do, how disputed it is. Don't confirm or refute them yourself. Text: [text]
prompts.eco.claims.refine: Write search queries to check claim [number].
prompts.eco.claims.check: For the claim [claim] I found this source: [source]. Is it suitable?
prompts.eco.report.short: Outline a report on the project [project].
prompts.eco.report.detailed: Help me put together a report on the project “[project]”. What we did: [what we did]. Results: [results]. Structure: problem, goal, what we did, data and results (with how they were obtained), what didn't work and why, conclusions, next steps, acknowledgements (by role). Give prompts for each section, not finished text.
prompts.eco.report.refine: Make a one-page summary of the report for the school website.
prompts.eco.report.check: Here's the results section: [text]. Can you tell from it how the numbers were obtained?

verify.eco.problem: Check the problem really exists where you are: look for yourself, ask people, find data.
verify.eco.data: Record how and when you collected the data: without that it can't be checked or compared.
verify.eco.survey: Test the survey on 2–3 people before launching: unclear questions give useless answers.
verify.eco.campaign: Back every fact in campaign materials with a source. Scare tactics without facts undermine trust.
verify.eco.materials: Check the materials are safe for participants, especially children, and whether you can get them without buying.
verify.eco.solutions: Take data on how well solutions work from research and official reports, not from the AI's estimates.
verify.eco.volunteer: Agree the event with the venue's administration and responsible adults. Take care of participants' safety.
verify.eco.conclusions: Don't draw broad conclusions from a small sample. State how much data you have and where it's from.
verify.eco.claims: Check environmental figures against official statistics and scientific sources: there are many inflated numbers online.
verify.eco.report: Describe honestly what didn't work in the report: that's as valuable as the successes.
